subject: history
title: Great Patriotic War and Postwar Stalinism
welcome_lead: From Barbarossa to the Doctors' Plot, 1941-53.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on Soviet WWII, postwar repression and the Eastern Bloc.
final_note: You have walked from Stalingrad to Stalin's deathbed.

concepts.def: Soviet term for the war against Nazi Germany, 22 June 1941 to 9 May 1945, costing about 27 million Soviet lives.
Stalin's 'Not One Step Back' order of 28 July 1942 introducing penal battalions and blocking detachments.
Battle from August 1942 ending 2 February 1943 with surrender of Paulus's Sixth Army.
Conferences (February and July-August 1945) shaping postwar Europe and Soviet sphere.
Postwar cultural campaign 1946-48 under Andrei Zhdanov enforcing socialist realism and anti-cosmopolitanism.
Antisemitic conspiracy fabricated in January 1953 accusing Jewish doctors of plotting against Soviet leaders.

walkthroughs.body_html: Operation Barbarossa launched on 22 June 1941 captured 3 million Soviet POWs and reached the gates of Moscow by December. Soviet recovery, US Lend-Lease (about USD 11 billion) and German overextension allowed counter-offensives. Order 227 of 28 July 1942 stiffened defence. Stalingrad's surrender in February 1943 ended Wehrmacht offensive capacity, followed by Kursk in July 1943.

walkthroughs.h2: Eastern Bloc and Cold War onset
walkthroughs.body_html: Red Army occupation enabled installation of communist regimes in Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary, East Germany and Czechoslovakia by 1948. The Cominform formed in September 1947 to coordinate parties. Yugoslavia split with Stalin in 1948. Comecon (1949) and Warsaw Pact (1955) institutionalised the bloc. The Berlin Blockade of 1948-49 marked the deepening of confrontation.

Postwar repression renewed: the Leningrad Affair (1949-51) executed regional leaders. The Mingrelian Affair (1951) targeted Beria's Georgian network. The January 1953 Doctors' Plot fed antisemitic paranoia. Stalin's stroke on 1 March and death on 5 March 1953 prompted collective leadership. Khrushchev's 'Secret Speech' of February 1956 inaugurated de-Stalinisation.
